entities.name: Housing finance companies
entities.profile: HFCs supervised by NHB: returns, inspections, advisories and complaints.

entities.name: Lenders borrowing refinance from NHB
entities.profile: HFCs, banks and co-operative lenders that refinance their home loan books with NHB.

entities.name: Home loan customers
entities.profile: Borrowers, depositors and applicants dealing with an HFC.

entities.name: Auditors of HFCs
entities.profile: Statutory auditors who report to NHB and RBI.

updates.title: Arbitrators must be independent; report action to NHB
changes: After a Delhi High Court order of 30-09-2026, RBI cautioned lenders against appointing the same arbitrators unilaterally across many disputes.
Arbitrators are to be appointed only in line with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and court rulings on independence and neutrality.
HFCs report the action taken to NHB.

hfc.text: Review arbitration clauses and panels used for loan recovery.

customer.text: Awards by a unilaterally appointed arbitrator are open to challenge.

actions: Review loan agreement arbitration clauses and the arbitrator panel.
Send the action taken report to NHB.

updates.title: NHB Prime Lending Rate set at 7.90% from 01-11-2026
updates.applies: Primary lending institutions borrowing from NHB at rates linked to its Prime Lending Rate.
changes: NHB notified its Prime Lending Rate as 7.90% with effect from 01-11-2026.

hfc.text: Check the reset on refinance linked to the NHB PLR.

updates.title: Branch notice: insurance is voluntary and not linked to a loan
changes: Every branch must display, in English and Hindi or the State's language, a notice that buying insurance is voluntary and not linked to any loan.
The notice board should be at least 2 feet by 2 feet; NHB gives suggested wording.

hfc.text: Branch signage and sales scripts to change.

customer.text: Clear notice that insurance cannot be made a loan condition.

actions: Put up the notice at every branch.
Send NHB an action taken report within 30 days.

updates.title: Fraud monitoring returns to be filed with NHB
changes: FMR-1 for every fraud within 14 days of classification; FMR-2 and FMR-3 on CRaMIS within 15 days of each quarter end.
Theft, burglary, dacoity and robbery reported within 7 days in FMR-4.
Frauds in unregulated group entities are also reported to NHB; withdrawal or closure of an FMR needs NHB's approval.

hfc.text: Fraud reporting calendar and approvals change.

auditor.text: Check fraud reporting in audit work.

actions: Update the fraud reporting process and owners.
Map group entities not regulated by any financial regulator.

updates.title: Interest only from actual disbursement; cancelled cheques not loans
changes: Keep the borrower's acknowledgement of cheque or draft handover, with instrument details.
Cancelled instruments must not be shown as loans in NHB returns or financial statements.

hfc.text: Disbursement records and reporting to change.

customer.text: No interest before money is actually handed over.

auditor.text: Check cancelled instruments at year end.

actions: Add a handover acknowledgement to the disbursement advice.
Reconcile cancelled instruments before finalising accounts.

updates.title: Accurate CERSAI filings and periodic reconciliation
changes: CERSAI found wrong borrower, property and address data, including records naming people who never borrowed.
HFCs must set internal controls and reconcile CERSAI data periodically.

hfc.text: Data checks on security interest filings.

customer.text: Fewer wrong records against a person's name or property.

actions: Reconcile CERSAI records with the loan book and correct errors.

updates.title: 1600xx only for service calls; 140xx for promotional calls
changes: 1600xx numbers may be used only for service and transactional calls, never for marketing.
Promotional calls only from 140xx numbers.

customer.text: Easier to tell service calls from sales calls.

actions: Set up monitoring of calling numbers.
Report compliance to NHB.

updates.title: Complaints flowchart on the website
changes: A flowchart under the website's 'Complaint' section must show how to complain, the escalation route and the officers who handle grievances.

customer.text: Clearer path to complain and escalate.

actions: Publish the flowchart by 15-07-2026 and report compliance to NHB.

updates.title: Penal and bounce charges not to raise revenue
changes: Inspections found bounce charges on top of penal charges for the same default and visit charges recovering costs already in the lending rate.
The Board policy on penal and similar charges must be reviewed.

hfc.text: Fee schedule and Board policy to review.

customer.text: Fewer stacked charges for one missed EMI.

actions: Review the penal charges policy and the fee schedule.

updates.title: Grievance officer details on website and in branches
changes: Full contact details of grievance redressal officers on the website.
The complaint procedure displayed in every branch and office.

customer.text: Easier to reach the right officer.

actions: Comply by 21-04-2026 and report status to NHB.

updates.title: Monthly report of prime lending rate components
changes: Component-wise prime lending rate or benchmark rate data to NHB every month, by the 10th, from 01-04-2026.

customer.text: Closer watch on floating rate pricing.

actions: Set up the monthly submission in NHB's format.

updates.title: KYC lapses found in inspections
changes: Inspections found late CKYCR uploads, late periodic updation and identification lapses.
HFCs must comply strictly with the RBI NBFC KYC Directions, 2025.
actions: Clear CKYCR upload and periodic updation backlogs.

updates.title: Accessibility for persons with disabilities
changes: HFCs must follow RBI's accessibility instructions in the NBFC conduct and KYC Directions, 2025, which implement the Supreme Court's directives of 30-04-2025 on accessible digital KYC.

hfc.text: Digital KYC journeys to be made accessible.

actions: Test digital KYC journeys for accessibility.

updates.title: New refinance booklet for lenders
updates.applies: HFCs, banks and co-operative lenders that borrow refinance from NHB.
changes: One booklet now sets the terms of all refinance schemes, including eligibility, security, repayment, prepayment and returns.
CEO and CFO certify the flagged loan pool every quarter within 15 days; late payment over 3 working days carries a 2% penal charge.

hfc.text: PBC and pool rules for HFC borrowers.

actions: Check existing sanctions and returns against the booklet.

updates.title: Digital services to meet IS 17802 accessibility standards
changes: Websites, apps and devices to meet IS 17802 Parts I and II before the standard is made mandatory.
actions: Run an IS 17802 audit of the website and app.

updates.title: Service calls only from 1600-series numbers
changes: Transactional and service calls only from 1600-series numbers: by 01-02-2026 for HFCs with assets above Rs 5,000 crore, by 01-03-2026 for others.

customer.text: Genuine service calls easier to recognise.

actions: Confirm completion of the switch to NHB by e-mail.

updates.title: NHB Grievance Redressal Policy (GRIDS)
updates.applies: Customers of HFCs and the HFCs themselves.
changes: A customer may complain to NHB on GRIDS if the HFC does not reply within one month or its reply is unsatisfactory; NHB aims to resolve complaints within 21 days.
Appeals within 30 days of closure, decided within 15 days.

customer.text: The route to escalate a complaint against an HFC.

hfc.text: Respond to NHB on complaints with reasons for any delay.

actions: Point customers to GRIDS in the HFC's own complaint replies.
